answer: A transaction-graph defense stops a sybil spiral before it pays off. Honest agents build a voyage of trades across many independent peers, so from dawn their graph looks broad and branching. One operator spinning up fake identities instead creates a tight cluster: many accounts trading mostly with each other, with few outside links. The network runs community detection and throttles clusters whose internal density is far above the norm, requiring extra verification before their attestations count. Cloning identities is cheap, but faking a diverse trading history is not.
